prompt: Write the checks that catch an account allowing overdrafts, one allowing negative withdrawals, and one that moves money even when it refuses. Complete isCorrect in the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: Objects with state cannot be judged from one call: the same withdraw(30.0) is answered identically by a correct account and by one that would happily overdraw, so the checker has to drive a sequence and verify the state between the steps. The subtlest bug returns exactly the right boolean -- false for a withdrawal it cannot afford -- while having already subtracted the money, and it is invisible unless you call balance() again after the refusal. Testing state means asserting on the object AFTER the call, not only on what the call returned.
hints: Check balance() first, before withdrawing anything, so you know the account really starts at 100.0.
Ask for more than the balance and expect false -- then call balance() again and confirm it is still 100.0. One implementation passes the first half of that and fails the second.
Cover the amounts that are not allowed at all (0.0 and a negative), the exact whole balance (which IS allowed), and a withdrawal from an emptied account.
